collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The leader took extra fish from the shared catch for their own family: call it out, or speak to them privately.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) keeps the tally of the shared catch, and for a month the numbers have been wrong: the {@chief}'s family always takes a few more fish than everyone else. (subject) has told (friend), who says the {@chief} works hard and deserves a little extra. (subject) says nobody voted for that. What should (subject) do?

choices.label: Call It Out at the Gathering

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) shows the tally at the gathering. The {@chief} goes red, and says (other.his/her) family is large and (other.he/she) did not think anyone would mind. The village minds. The {@chief} agrees to take a fair share from now on. Some people trust the {@chief} a little less.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) goes to the {@chief} quietly. The {@chief} is embarrassed and promises to stop. And does. Nobody else ever knows. (subject) is not sure whether that was kind or whether the village had a right to know.
